title: Decode the toaster
prompt:
The talking toaster flashes three patterns of eight switches. Each pattern is one letter in ASCII. The first line of `toaster.py` already decodes the first one.

Add two lines that decode `01001111` and `01010100` the same way. Run `python3 toaster.py` to read the toaster's message, then run the tests.
hints: Copy the first `print` line twice. Each copy needs a different pattern of 0s and 1s.
Change only the text inside the quotes. Keep `base=2`, because the pattern is binary.
The new lines are `print(chr(int("01001111", base=2)))` and `print(chr(int("01010100", base=2)))`.
explain_after: `int("01001111", base=2)` read the switches as a base-2 number [py-039], and `chr()` turned the number into its character, the inverse of `ord()` [py-040]. The toaster is warning you that it is hot.
